Topics · Is the Quran from God?

Did the Quran truly foretell Rome's victory?

When Persia beat Rome, the Quran said Rome would win in a few years. Historians, and the strongest objection.

Part 1 of 3

﴿غُلِبَتِ ٱلرُّومُ٢ فِىٓ أَدْنَى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَهُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ٣ فِى بِضْعِ سِنِينَ ۗ لِلَّهِ ٱلْأَمْرُ مِن قَبْلُ وَمِنۢ بَعْدُ ۚ وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ٤﴾

Translation of the meaning

The Byzantines have been defeated[1139] In the nearest land.[1140] But they, after their defeat, will overcome Within three to nine years. To Allāh belongs the command [i.e., decree] before and after. And that day the believers will rejoice

Translator's notes

[1139] By the Persians.

[1140] Another meaning is "in the lowest land."

Quran · Ar-Rum 30:2-4

Start with what the verses say, in plain terms. The Romans have been defeated. After their defeat they will win, within a few years. On that day the believers will be glad. Three things: a fact already true, a forecast, and a time frame. Everything turns on one question: when was this said, and how likely did the forecast look then?

A question for you

At the moment a forecast is made, what makes it worth taking seriously?

If you sayThat it looks very unlikely.
ThenThat is one mark: a forecast that sounds safe tells us little. The next part asks how unlikely this one looked.
If you sayThat it is specific about time.
ThenAnother good mark. Here the time is loose, a few years, and what follows says what that does to the weight.
If you sayThat the speaker risks something.
ThenYes. A forecast made in public can be shown wrong, which is part of what makes it count.

Part 2 of 3

﴿فِىٓ أَدْنَى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَهُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ٣ فِى بِضْعِ سِنِينَ ۗ لِلَّهِ ٱلْأَمْرُ مِن قَبْلُ وَمِنۢ بَعْدُ ۚ وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ٤﴾

Translation of the meaning

In the nearest land.[1140] But they, after their defeat, will overcome Within three to nine years. To Allāh belongs the command [i.e., decree] before and after. And that day the believers will rejoice

Translator's notes

[1140] Another meaning is "in the lowest land."

Quran · Ar-Rum 30:3-4

The historian Edward Gibbon, who did not accept this prophecy, wrote that when it is said to have been given, nothing looked further from fulfilment: the empire's early troubles pointed to its end. Then events turned. From 622 the emperor counter-attacked, and by 627 and 628 the Persian king was beaten and deposed. ‘A few years’ is flexible, and scholars differ on which events count.

A question for you

How much weight would you give a forecast like this?

If you sayA lot, if the dates hold.
ThenThat is the right place to press. The dates are the strongest and the most debated part, and scholars discuss them openly.
If you saySome, but it is not decisive.
ThenA fair weight, and close to where this Step ends: a sign scholars discuss, not a proof.
If you sayNone. A lucky guess is possible.
ThenIt is possible, and you are entitled to say so. The next part gives the strongest version of that objection.

Part 3 of 3

﴿بِنَصْرِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ يَنصُرُ مَن يَشَآءُ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ٥ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ ۖ لَا يُخْلِفُ ٱللَّهُ وَعْدَهُۥ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ٦﴾

Translation of the meaning

In the victory of Allāh.[1141] He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. [It is] the promise of Allāh. Allāh does not fail in His promise, but most of the people do not know.

Translator's notes

[1141] i.e., the victory given by Allāh to a people of the Scripture (Christians) over the Magians of Persia.

Quran · Ar-Rum 30:5-6

Translation

God is not a man, that he should lie, nor a son of man, that he should repent. Has he said, and he won’t do it? Or has he spoken, and he won’t make it good?

Original · Hebrew

לֹ֣א אִ֥ישׁ אֵל֙ וִֽיכַזֵּ֔ב וּבֶן־אָדָ֖ם וְיִתְנֶחָ֑ם הַה֤וּא אָמַר֙ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְדִבֶּ֖ר וְלֹ֥א יְקִימֶֽנָּה׃

the Torah (Numbers) · 23:19

World English Bible

The strongest objection: the two empires had traded blows for centuries, so a Roman recovery was not mad for someone who knew that history, and ‘a few years’ is loose enough to fit several outcomes. A second point: the date of the chapter comes from tradition. The strongest reply: it was said openly, when the empire was at its lowest, so a failure would have been seen by everyone. You can hold both.

A question for you

What size would you give this sign?

If you saySmall, but real.
ThenA common and honest weight. It means: worth noting, not enough alone.
If you saySubstantial.
ThenThen keep the against column in view. The weight you give should survive those points.
If you sayI need more before I say.
ThenReasonable. This is one sign among several, and the others do not depend on this one.

Your reflection

What is the last forecast you heard that looked hopeless when it was made? How did you decide whether to take it seriously?
